findings.text: non-blocking: section 8 states that when a later change removes a branch the row naming it no longer resolves, and the evidence fragment repeats that a later edit moving the code under a row fails the check; but docs/research/where-behaviour-follows-a-backends-name.check.py:66 takes the revision from the record's own plan-measured-at meta and resolves every row against that pinned revision (check.py:44), so a commit that later moves or removes code cannot change what git show returns for the pinned revision and cannot make any row fail. The check guards the record against edits that break row resolution, not against code drift, and the record overstates that guarantee.
